q: The puffed-up appearance of idli and dosa dough is due to:
CO2 produced by bacteria fermenting the dough
Dosa and idli dough is fermented by bacteria, which produce CO2 gas and give it a puffed-up appearance.
Baker’s yeast used for fermenting bread dough is:
The dough used for making bread is fermented using baker’s yeast, Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
Industrial-scale production of microbial products requires growing microbes in large vessels called:
Production on an industrial scale requires growing microbes in very large vessels called fermentors.
Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin while he was working on cultures of:
Fleming was working on Staphylococci bacteria when he noticed a mould on an unwashed culture plate around which the Staphylococci could not grow.
Cyclosporin A and statins are respectively obtained from:
Cyclosporin A is produced by the fungus Trichoderma polysporum and statins by the yeast Monascus purpureus.
A small part of the activated sludge is pumped back into the aeration tank. Its role there is to act as:
A settling aid to remove grit
A small part of the activated sludge is pumped back into the aeration tank to serve as the inoculum, seeding the incoming effluent with the required aerobic microbes.
Methanogens produce large amounts of methane along with:
Methanogens growing anaerobically on cellulosic material produce large amounts of methane along with CO2 and H2.
In a biogas plant, the structure that rises as gas accumulates is the:
Floating cover placed over the slurry
A floating cover is placed over the slurry; it keeps on rising as gas is produced in the tank by microbial activity.
Bacillus thuringiensis is used as a biocontrol agent chiefly against:
Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) is sprayed as dried spores to control butterfly caterpillars; the spores reach the gut of the larvae and kill them.
The fungus that lives in the roots of plants and acts as a biocontrol agent against several plant pathogens is:
Trichoderma, a free-living fungus common in root ecosystems, is an effective biocontrol agent of several plant pathogens. Glomus forms mycorrhiza (biofertiliser),…
Rhizobium acts as a biofertilizer by living in symbiotic association with:
Rhizobium lives symbiotically in the root nodules of leguminous plants and fixes atmospheric nitrogen there.
Nostoc and Anabaena are important biofertilizers mainly in:
Cyanobacteria such as Nostoc and Anabaena fix atmospheric nitrogen and act as biofertilizers especially in paddy fields.
Roquefort cheese obtains its characteristic flavour because it is:
Ripened by growing a specific fungus on it
Injected with CO2 gas during storage
Roquefort cheese is ripened by growing a specific fungus on it, which gives the cheese its particular flavour.
In the human stomach, Lactic Acid Bacteria (LAB) are beneficial mainly because they:
Digest all the fats present in food
Play a role in checking disease-causing microbes
Convert stomach acid into lactic acid
Produce vitamin B12 exclusively for the liver
In our stomach too, LAB play a very beneficial role in checking disease-causing microbes.
When a small amount of curd is added to warm milk to make more curd, this added curd functions as a/an:
A small amount of curd added to warm milk for curdling acts as an inoculum (or starter) - it contains thousands of LAB which multiply rapidly in the fresh milk.
Microbes can survive in extreme environments such as deep inside geysers (thermal vents) at temperatures as high as:
Microbes survive even where no other life-form could exist - deep inside geysers (thermal vents) at temperatures as high as 100°C.
Bacteria and many fungi can be grown on nutritive media to form structures useful for studying micro-organisms. These structures are called:
Bacteria and many fungi can be grown on nutritive media to form colonies that are visible to the naked eye; such cultures are useful in studies on micro-organisms.
Chemical substances produced by some microbes, which can kill or retard the growth of other disease-causing microbes, are called:
Antibiotics (Gr. anti = against; bios = life) are chemical substances produced by some microbes which can kill or retard the growth of other (disease-causing) microbes.
Whisky, brandy and rum have a much higher alcohol content than wine and beer because they are:
Made from malted cereals instead of fruit juices
Fermented for a much shorter duration
Fermented using a different yeast species
Produced by distillation of the fermented broth
Whisky, brandy and rum are produced by distillation of the fermented broth - distillation concentrates the alcohol, so these drinks have a much higher alcohol content.
The enzyme lipase, produced by microbes, is widely used in laundry detergents mainly because it:
Digests fats and helps remove oily stains
Breaks down pectin in cloth fibres
Lipase is used in laundry detergents; it digests fats and so helps in removing oily stains from the laundry.
During primary treatment of sewage, floating debris such as rags, plastics and sticks is first removed by:
Initially, sequential filtration removes the floating debris (rags, plastics, sticks, paper) during primary treatment.
Soil and small pebbles (grit) present in sewage are removed during primary treatment by:
Grit - soil and small pebbles - is removed by sedimentation in a grit chamber during primary treatment.
In the primary settling tank, the solids that settle down form the primary sludge, while the liquid standing above it is called:
All the solids that settle down in the primary settling tank form the primary sludge, while the liquid that stands above it is the supernatant, called the primary…
The type of gas produced by microbial activity depends on two factors: the substrate on which the microbes grow, and the:
Colour of the floating gas holder
Type of microbe growing on it
The type of gas produced depends on two things: (a) the substrate (the material) on which the microbes grow, and (b) the type of microbe growing on it.
The digester tank of a typical gobar gas plant is a concrete tank sunk into the ground to a depth of about:
The plant consists of a concrete tank, 10-15 feet deep, sunk in the ground, in which bio-wastes are collected and a slurry of dung is fed.
In a biogas plant, the gas produced is supplied to nearby houses through the:
The plant has an outlet which is connected to a pipe that supplies the biogas to nearby houses.
Biogas produced in a gobar gas plant is mainly used in rural homes for:
The biogas produced is used for cooking and lighting in homes.
Ladybird beetles are used as biocontrol agents mainly to get rid of:
Ladybird beetles (ladybirds) are used to get rid of aphids.
Dragonflies are used as natural predators to control:
Dragonflies are used to get rid of mosquitoes.
Different cry genes of Bacillus thuringiensis act on different pests; the gene cryIAb, for example, is specifically effective against:
Different cry genes act on different pests (cryIAc and cryIIAb against cotton bollworms, cryIAb against corn borer).
Azospirillum and Azotobacter enrich soil nitrogen content by fixing atmospheric nitrogen while:
Living inside paddy field water only
Living inside root nodules of legumes
Some other bacteria such as Azospirillum and Azotobacter can fix atmospheric nitrogen while free-living in the soil, thus also enriching its nitrogen content.
Anabaena, a nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium, is found inside the leaf cavities of which plant grown as a green biofertilizer in paddy fields?
Anabaena is also found inside the leaf cavities of the water fern Azolla, which is grown in paddy fields as a green biofertilizer.
Besides resistance to root-borne pathogens, plants with mycorrhizal associations also show increased tolerance to:
Plants having mycorrhizal associations show other benefits too - resistance to root-borne pathogens, tolerance to salinity and drought, and an overall increase in…
Compared to chemical fertilizers, biofertilizers are best described as:
Effective only on large industrial farms
Biofertilizers are cheap, renewable and non-polluting, and unlike chemical fertilizers they improve soil texture and soil life instead of damaging it.
Excessive use of chemical fertilizers contributes heavily to pollution of:
Only crop seeds stored for the next season
Soil, ground water and water bodies
Chemical fertilizers increase crop yield, but their excessive use contributes heavily to pollution of soil, ground water and water bodies.
Rhizobium fixes atmospheric nitrogen for the plant only when it is:
Inside the leaf cavities of Azolla
Inside the root nodule of a leguminous plant
Rhizobium fixes nitrogen only when it is inside the nodule; while free-living in the soil it does not fix nitrogen.
A small amount of curd added to warm milk brings about curdling because it acts as:
A catalyst that lowers activation energy
A source of vitamin B12 for the milk
An inoculum containing thousands of LAB
The small amount of curd added to milk acts as an inoculum containing thousands of LAB, which multiply further and curdle the milk.
Toddy, a traditional drink of some parts of southern India, is prepared by fermenting:
Toddy is made by fermenting sap obtained from palms.
Streptokinase, produced by Streptococcus, is used as a:
Streptokinase is used as a clot buster to remove clots from the blood vessels of patients who have undergone myocardial infarction leading to heart attack.
Fleming, Chain and Florey were awarded the Nobel Prize in 1945 for their work on:
Penicillin was the first antibiotic discovered by Alexander Fleming; Ernest Chain and Howard Florey established its full potential as an effective antibiotic, and all…
The sediment of bacterial flocs that settles down in the settling tank during secondary treatment of sewage is called:
After BOD is reduced significantly, the effluent is passed into a settling tank where the bacterial flocs sediment; this sediment is called activated sludge.
Methanogens grow anaerobically on cellulosic material and produce methane along with CO2 and H2.
The technology of biogas production was developed in India mainly due to the efforts of:
Biogas technology in India was developed mainly through the efforts of the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) and the Khadi and Village Industries…
Dried spores of which organism are sold in sachets and sprayed on crops to control caterpillars?
Bacillus thuringiensis is available in sachets as dried spores which are sprayed on the crop; the spores enter the gut of the larvae and kill them.
Symbiotic association of a fungus with the roots of higher plants, which helps in absorption of phosphorus, is called:
Mycorrhiza is the symbiotic association between a fungus (for example Glomus) and plant roots; the fungal partner absorbs phosphorus and passes it to the plant.
The vitamin whose content in milk increases when Lactic Acid Bacteria (LAB) convert it into curd is:
LAB improve the nutritional quality of the product by increasing the amount of vitamin B12 during the conversion of milk into curd.
The bacterium used for the commercial production of acetic acid is:
Acetobacter aceti (a bacterium) is used for the commercial and industrial production of acetic acid.
Grit (soil and small pebbles) present in sewage is removed during primary treatment by:
Grit - soil and small pebbles - is removed by sedimentation in a grit chamber during primary treatment.
The spent slurry removed from a biogas plant is best used as:
A disinfectant for the digester tank
Fertiliser, since it is rich in nutrients
The spent slurry removed from a biogas plant is not waste - it is rich in nutrients and may be used as fertiliser.
The cry genes of Bacillus thuringiensis, responsible for killing insect larvae, have been introduced into plants using:
Using genetic engineering, the genes of B. thuringiensis responsible for killing the larvae (cry genes) have been introduced into plants themselves, giving Bt-cotton.
Bacteria such as Azospirillum and Azotobacter enrich soil nitrogen content by fixing atmospheric nitrogen while:
Living inside root nodules of legumes
Living inside the leaf cavities of Azolla
Azospirillum and Azotobacter can fix atmospheric nitrogen while free-living in the soil, thus enriching its nitrogen content.
